review_notes: The file is one huge term-mode certificate with no simp lemmas or attributes of its own. The only simp interface it touches is eight `by simp only [fv_syn_c1c/c0/cnnc]` side-goals, plus `by decide` calls. I read the `fv_syn_*` definitions in CompactSyntaxFVExplicit.lean and the parallel CompactSyntaxFV.lean. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say whether these `simp only` calls would work with `@[simp]` lemmas or what the effect on other files would be. The finding is a modest interface inconsistency, not a failure. I did not check every downstream use of the Explicit lemmas.

findings.problem: The file opens `NFChoice.Compiler.CompactSyntaxFVExplicit` and uses its `fv_syn_c1c`, `fv_syn_c0` and `fv_syn_cnnc`. In that file these closed-class free-variable lemmas have no `@[simp]` attribute, and the file has no simp attributes at all. The sibling file `CompactSyntaxFV.lean` has the same statements, e.g. `fv_syn_c1c : (synC1c).fv = (∅ : Finset Var)`, marked `@[simp]`. The two parallel copies therefore disagree on simp behaviour. Callers of the Explicit versions must name every lemma by hand: here eight times in this file (lines 242, 434, 660, 724, 900, 1096, 1326, 1390), and in many other files via `simp only [...]` or `simp [..., fv_syn_c0, ...]`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the closed-term lemmas `fv_syn_c0`, `fv_syn_c1c` and `fv_syn_cnnc` in CompactSyntaxFVExplicit.lean `@[simp]`, as the CompactSyntaxFV copy already does. Also mark the other `fv_syn_*` lemmas whose right-hand side is `∅` or a union of argument free-variable sets. These oriented rules shrink the term and cannot loop. Side goals like `(synC1c).fv = ∅` could then be closed by plain `simp`, with no per-site lemma lists. Alternatively, remove the duplicate copy so that only one simp-tagged family exists.
findings.benefit: Callers get one canonical simp normal form for `.fv` of the syntactic constants. The certificates need no hand-written lemma lists, and the two parallel files cannot drift apart on simp behaviour.

evidence.excerpt: simp [synCplc, fv_syn_c0, fv_syn_cin, fv_syn_cun, fv_syn_wa, fv_syn_wrex, Wff.fv,
